component.name: OnionDesk
component.summary: Modern Tor client with a live circuit visualizer, country exits and a private browser

description.p: OnionDesk is a free and open-source Tor client with a modern interface and a live circuit visualizer (guard, middle, exit on a world map). It starts a bundled Tor client with a strict exit relay in the country you pick, shows your real and exit locations on a live world map, and ranks countries by live speed estimates. No account, no subscription, no telemetry.

ul.li: Choose a country exit, or turn on Auto to always use the fastest location
Switch location while the proxy stays up (designed so your real IP is not exposed during the change)
Live world map with animated pins for your real and exit IP
Optional system-wide mode that sends all TCP and DNS traffic from every app through Tor (asks for administrator permission once)
Crash-safety by design: your normal network settings are restored automatically on the next start, or with the oniondesk-restore command, if the app is killed
I2P tab (beta) with a bundled i2pd router and per-app split tunneling, for .i2p sites
OnionDesk Browser (beta): tabs and full view inside the app, using Tor for the web and I2P for .i2p, with no direct connection
Leak test, circuit visualizer, bridges (obfs4, Snowflake, meek), ad blocker, new identity and auto-rotate
Tor is bundled, so there is nothing else to install

description.p: By default it is a local SOCKS5 proxy, so only apps that honour the system proxy are covered. Tor is slower than a commercial VPN and cannot carry UDP traffic. OnionDesk is not affiliated with the Tor Project, I2P or Google. It is not a VPN service and does not guarantee anonymity; your behaviour and unencrypted traffic can still identify you. It does not collect data, but it contacts third-party services (for example to look up your IP address); see the privacy policy. You are responsible for following the laws that apply to you.
Testers welcome: please try it on your distribution and report what works and what does not (bugs, ideas, your distribution and desktop) at the issue tracker or by email.
Privacy policy, legal notices and security policy inside the app; signed apt and dnf repositories; more careful wording of what the app does and does not guarantee. See the release notes on GitHub.
